key_insight: Train a Vision Transformer (ViT) to directly predict language tokens from visual tokens with a standard autoregressive language-modeling objective, enabling a minimalist, generative vision encoder that naturally aligns with autoregressive LLMs.
problem_solved: Bridges the architectural and objective mismatch between vision encoders and autoregressive LLMs, avoiding complex contrastive pipelines or extra text decoders during multimodal pretraining.
method: Use ViT as a generative encoder that maps visual tokens to language tokens and is trained with a standard language modeling loss (autoregressive token prediction).
Adopt a minimalist pretraining pipeline that omits contrastive batch construction and separate text decoders, simplifying training and integration.
Align the vision encoder’s outputs to be compatible with downstream MLLMs so the visual component 'speaks' the same token language as the LLM.
impact: Simplifies multimodal pretraining and improves compatibility between vision encoders and autoregressive LLMs, reducing engineering complexity and making it easier to build efficient multimodal LLMs.
visual_elements: Architecture flow: image → ViT (visual tokens) → autoregressive language token prediction → LLM consumption

paper_title: Let ViT Speak: Generative Language-Image Pre-training
